content.title: About
content.content: Egg salad with Italian dressing is a classic American dish from the early 1960s. Core ingredients are hard‑boiled eggs, mayonnaise, mustard and a fragrant Italian dressing made from olive oil, vinegar, oregano, basil and garlic. Served cold as a snack or light meal.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish first appeared in the United States in the early 1960s as Italian cuisine gained popularity.
The Italian dressing gives the salad a distinctive herbaceous flavor compared to the plain mayo‑only egg salad.
It is often used as a filling for sandwiches and baguettes.
Modern recipes sometimes add chopped pickles or celery for extra crunch.
The 1961 recipe was featured in magazines such as Better Homes and Gardens and Cook’s Illustrated.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Eggs provide a complete source of protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Contains healthy fats
items.content: Olive oil in the dressing supplies monounsaturated fatty acids that support heart health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs are rich in B2, B6 and B12, which are important for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Herbs (oregano, basil) and garlic contain polyphenols with antioxidant properties.

items.title: Bone support
items.content: Eggs and olive oil provide modest amounts of vitamin D and calcium, beneficial for bone health.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Raw or undercooked eggs may harbor salmonella; always use fully cooked eggs.

items.title: Calorie dense
items.content: Mayonnaise and olive oil make the dish high in calories, so watch portion sizes.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: People with egg allergy can experience mild to severe reactions.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Eggs contain cholesterol; those with high blood cholesterol should consume in moderation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve chilled as a dip, in salad bowls, or on crackers. It also works well as a sandwich filling, on toast, or as a side to vegetable dishes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Stir before serving to redistribute the dressing.
